The outer upper side is labeled as three segments, 5 m, 2 m, 5 m, so the outer upper base is 12 m; the lower base is labeled 8 m. The opening above the notch is 2 m, and the two slanted sides are each labeled 6 m. The vertical distance from the vertex of the notch to the bottom side is labeled 1 m. Reasoning: According to the specified method, regard the shaded part as the large outer trapezoid minus the middle triangular notch. The notch is an isosceles triangle, and the 2 m opening is bisected into the bases of two 1 m right triangles. The notch height is sqrt(6^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(35). The height of the outer trapezoid is sqrt(35) + 1. The area of the outer trapezoid is ((12 + 8) / 2)(sqrt(35) + 1) = 10(sqrt(35) + 1). The area of the notch triangle is (1/2)(2)(sqrt(35)) = sqrt(35). The shaded area is 10(sqrt(35) + 1) - sqrt(35) = 9sqrt(35) + 10 ≈ 63.2445, rounded to the nearest tenth is 63.2.

From the image, read the outer top as 5 m + 2 m + 5 m = 12 m, the bottom base as 8 m, the two slanted sides of the central notch as 6 m each, the notch opening as 2 m, and the vertical distance from the notch vertex to the bottom base as 1 m. Since the notch is isosceles, split its 2 m top base into two 1 m halves; use the Pythagorean theorem to get the notch height sqrt(6^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(35). Therefore the outer trapezoid height is sqrt(35) + 1. Compute outer trapezoid area as ((12 + 8)/2)(sqrt(35)+1), subtract the notch triangle area (1/2)(2)(sqrt(35)), then round to the nearest tenth.
